The number of stars per unit range of parallax is derived from the volume distribution. For stars uniformly distributed in space (constant number density), the number of stars at distance \(d\) is proportional to the volume element \(d^2\, dd\). Parallax \(p\) is inversely proportional to distance: \(p \propto 1/d\), so \(d \propto 1/p\) and \(dd \propto dp/p^2\). Substituting gives the number per unit parallax: \(N(p)\, dp \propto (1/p)^2 \cdot (1/p^2)\, dp = p^{-4}\, dp\). Thus, \(N(p) \propto 1/p^4\).

Answer: C
